keyFindings.description: With the claim refreshed, a queued attempt is live (MentionLiveSQL) for its whole lane wait, so the outbox keeps that comment.created deferred (errMentionPending) and re-reads it every retry tick (~5 s) until the lane reaches it: 100 comments behind a silent listener stay deferred about 8 minutes, each re-polled. mentions.go:21-25 and 34-40 and AGENTS.md:3333-3337 still bound the deferral, and the edit-before-creation window hosts are told about, at about a minute; publisher.go:299-300 says the claim bounds it. Bound it (a claimed attempt older than a lease is treated as resumed: fallback row and publish) or back off the deferral and state the real bound.

wait() releases the unstarted claims on m.ctx (:355), which a timer cancels mentionDrainTimeout (10 s) after the lifetime ends (:166), while mentions.wait() runs last in waitBackground after the HTTP drain and document shutdown. A stop slower than 10 s logs an Error and leaves the claims to lapse instead of handing them over at once. Release on context.WithoutCancel(m.lifetime) with a timeout of its own.

On the held path (:214-216) a keyed repeat that re-claimed an attempt this process still queues does not record the new claim in m.claims, so later refreshes no-op on the row, the new claim lapses a lease later, and the sweep can send that attempt out of order. Set m.claims[key] to the new claim; also the refresh comment at :394 says an unmatched row is dropped, which the code does not do.

Round 4 asked for a test with a lane held longer than a lease while the sweep runs. The held-lane test (:857-917) ages only created_at and calls refreshHeldClaims directly; no claim gets older than a lease, so it passes with keepClaims deleted. Age claimed_at past the lease with and without a refresh (negative control) while a sweep pass runs.

A POST /api/v1/comments/{id}/deliveries while attempt 1 is queued now opens attempt 2, and the lane still sends attempt 1 (the bound path does not check MentionLatestAttemptSQL); in a different mode the keys differ and the recipient gets two copies. Only an API caller can do this (the UI retries failed attempts only); make the bound send skip an attempt that is no longer the latest, or refuse a retry of a pending claimed attempt. Prose in the same round: the 0142 migration header (next_attempt_at's waiting release), AGENTS.md:3286 MentionLiveSQL wording.
